implementation.declaration: extern "C" SporepediaOnlineAsset* SW1_00EC4280_THISCALL re_00ec4280(SporepediaOnlineAsset* receiver, std::uint8_t delete_flags);
implementation.argument_surface: receiver in ECX (copied into ESI at 0x00ec4281 and never moved back); exactly ONE ordinary stack argument in the 4-byte slot at entry_ESP+0x4, of which only the LOW BYTE is read. The byte read is fixed by the opcode form at 0x00ec429C: F6 44 24 08 01 is 0xF6 /0, the r/m8 TEST, with ModRM 0x44 (mod=01) and SIB 0x24 selecting ESP and a disp8 of +0x08. 0x00ec429C runs with ESP = entry-4 (the PUSH ESI at 0x00ec4280 is still in effect and 0x00642190 pops nothing), so [ESP+0x8] is entry+0x4, the argument slot. Ghidra's decompilation names the same two things (`param_1` = the receiver, `param_2` = a byte) and agrees on `return param_1`.
implementation.return_type_note: Ghidra's own record disagrees with its own decompilation here: ghidra_function.return_type is "undefined" and return_type_resolved is false, while the decompilation returns param_1. The listing settles it: 0x00ec42AC MOV EAX,ESI is on the SINGLE exit shared by both arms of the branch, and ESI has held the receiver since 0x00ec4281. The ABI record's return_semantics is the vacuous "unclassified_in_EAX"; this is the same fact read positively.
implementation.receiver_model: an opaque 0x18-byte run with NO members. The body reaches exactly three displacements on its receiver -- 0x00, 0x10, 0x14 -- and the machine-derived receiver record enumerates exactly those three (offsets [0, 16, 20], max_offset 20, register ECX, shape R-ALIAS, written_through 3, bounds_only true). 0x14 is the largest displacement touched and the stores are 4 bytes wide, so 0x18 is the last byte the body can write. No member is named for any displacement, because the record states where the body reached and not what anything is for; the three words are called vptrs here because the VALUES they receive are vftable bases (see mechanics.vtable_associations).
implementation.dispatch_model: none. The body contains no indirect transfer: abi_derived.dispatch records indirect_calls 0, call_offsets [] and vtable_shaped_loads 0, which agrees with a 14-instruction listing in which both transfers are direct immediates. The model therefore declares no slot boundary anywhere and reads no vtable word. The vtable association is recorded as EVIDENCE about the immediates, not as a modelled dispatch.
implementation.dependency_note: both direct callees are declared extern in the package header and defined as observers in the package's own model test; no other package's header is included. 0x00642190 and 0x00F47380 are not owned by this package. 0x00642190 already has a persisted reconstruction under a different normalized_symbol (reconstruction/metadata/pkg-sporepedia-safe-wave10/00642190.json, sporepedia_asset_destroy_00642190) and this package adopts that name so it does not invent a competing one; 0x00F47380 is named deallocate_00f47380, the name already used across the corpus (e.g. reconstruction/staging/pkg-app-services-wave6/app_services.hpp:39). This package asserts about either of them only what their own instruction bytes fix: terminator form, stack-argument shape, argument order, and the three vptr words each of them writes.

function_extent.note_on_a_near_miss: 0x00ec42A9 ADD ESP,0x4 is 3 bytes (83 C4 04), not 4. ModRM 0xC4 is mod=11 / reg=000 / rm=100, and mod=11 with rm=100 is ESP as a register operand on x86-32, so no SIB byte is required. Reading it as 4 bytes would push the following instructions' addresses off by one and corrupt the whole tail of the trace.

mechanics.body_shape: write three vptr words into the receiver at +0x00, +0x10 and +0x14; call 0x00642190 with the receiver in ECX and nothing pushed; test the caller's flag BYTE against 0x01; if the bit is set, push the receiver and call the cdecl free at 0x00F47380; return the receiver. Fourteen instructions, one conditional branch, two direct calls, no indirect transfer, no global access.

vtable_associations.0x01489090: written to receiver+0x00. Reading the image at 0x01489090 gives the word 0x00EC4280 -- this body's own entry point. So the immediate is not a bare constant: it is the base of a virtual function table whose slot +0x00 holds this body. On an x86-32 MSVC-style ABI slot +0x00 of a vftable is the scalar/vector deleting destructor, and the machine has therefore itself fixed that this body is one.
vtable_associations.0x0148907C: written to receiver+0x10. The same image read shows 0x00EC4280 also at 0x0148907C + 0x14, and 0x00EC4230 at 0x0148907C + 0x08.

neighbouring_thunks.0x00ec4230: 83 E9 10 / E9 48 00 00 00 -- SUB ECX,0x10 then JMP 0x00ec4280. 10 bytes, INT3-padded to 16.
neighbouring_thunks.0x00ec4240: 83 E9 14 / E9 38 00 00 00 -- SUB ECX,0x14 then JMP 0x00ec4280. 10 bytes, INT3-padded to 16.
neighbouring_thunks.why_this_matters: These are the two entries the xref record lists at 0x00ec4233 / 0x00ec4243 -- the addresses Ghidra reports are the DISPLACEMENT bytes inside the JMPs, not call sites. Their existence is independent corroboration of the 0x10 and 0x14 displacements from a second direction: this body is reached for a receiver whose vptr words sit at those two offsets. It is also a trap for the reconstruction, which is why test_callee_arguments_and_ordering() asserts that neither callee is ever given a pointer adjusted by 0x10 or 0x14 -- a copy of a thunk adjustment into this body would be wrong.
neighbouring_thunks.not_modelled: the thunks themselves are not modelled and the model declares no class hierarchy. Only the fact that they exist, and what their bytes say, is recorded.

mechanics.control_flow: exactly ONE conditional branch: JZ 0x00ec42AC at 0x00ec42A1 (opcode 0x74, rel8 +0x09, landing on body offset 0x2c = 0x00ec42AC). It is the join point of both arms: 0x00ec42AC..0x00ec42AF is reached by falling through the deleting arm and by taking the branch from the non-deleting arm, and there is no other branch, no loop and no indirect transfer. The JZ polarity is therefore fixed: the free runs when the mask is CLEAR, i.e. the free is taken when the tested bit is SET.
mechanics.branch_condition: TEST byte ptr [ESP+0x8],0x1 / JZ. The mask is the single immediate 0x01 and the operand is a single BYTE at [ESP+0x8]. Bit 0 of the caller's flag byte and ONLY bit 0 selects the deleting arm. Bits 1..7 are never examined by anything in this body and nothing here claims what they mean.

read_ordering.claim: the flag byte is read at 0x00ec429C, i.e. AFTER the call at 0x00ec4297 has returned, and AFTER all three vptr stores have run.
read_ordering.why_it_is_observable: 0x00642190 overwrites the same three words (+0x00, +0x10, +0x14) with its own immediates before it returns, so the value of the flag byte's surroundings is not what this body left there. A callee -- or the caller, through an aliased pointer -- that wrote the flag slot between 0x00ec4297 and 0x00ec429C would change which arm this body takes, and the original would see the new value.
read_ordering.how_the_model_preserves_it: a C++ compiler is free to hoist the read of a by-value parameter, so the model calls a declared hook (sw1_delete_flag_read_hook) at exactly the machine's read point instead of reading the parameter inline. With the hook null the parameter is used, which is the ordinary path. The model test installs a hook to (a) observe that the destroy call is already on the trace and that the object already carries the callee's vptr, and (b) override the value, which is the only way to falsify 'tests the incoming parameter on entry' as opposed to 'tests whatever is in the slot at 0x00ec429C'.
read_ordering.not_a_machine_global: the hook is instrumentation, declared in the package header. The complete 14-instruction listing names no data-segment address; the only absolute operand inside the body is the CALL immediates.

transient_vptr_stores.finding: all three vptr stores this body makes are unconditionally clobbered before the function returns, and are therefore dead with respect to the final state of the object.
transient_vptr_stores.evidence: 0x00642190 begins with C7 06 48 F6 3F 01 / C7 46 10 48 27 46 01 / C7 46 14 38 27 46 01 -- the same three displacements 0x00 / 0x10 / 0x14 with 0x013FF648, 0x01462748 and 0x01462738. It then tail-jumps to 0x006412A0, whose entire body is C7 41 14 58 C4 3E 01 / C7 41 10 38 B9 3E 01 / C7 01 58 37 40 01 / C3 -- the same three displacements a THIRD time, with 0x013EC458, 0x013EB938 and 0x01403758, and in the reverse order 0x14, 0x10, 0x00.
transient_vptr_stores.consequence: on return, the receiver's three vptr words hold 0x01403758 / 0x013EB938 / 0x013EC458, not 0x01489090 / 0x0148907C / 0x0148906C. The stores at 0x00ec4283..0x00ec4290 exist so that code running DURING the callee chain -- virtual calls, the handle releases at 0x006421A7..0x00642202 -- sees this class's vtable rather than whatever was there before.
transient_vptr_stores.how_the_test_handles_it: the final vptr VALUES are a property of 0x00642190 and 0x006412A0, which are other packages' targets, so the model test does not assert them as a property of this reconstruction. What it does assert is (a) what the destroy callee saw ON ENTRY, which is where this body's three immediates are observable at all, and (b) that this body does not re-apply its own immediates after the call returns. The three callee constants are separately checked against the callee's own bytes.

mechanics.return_semantics_machine: EAX = ESI = the receiver at 0x00ec42AC, on the single exit shared by both arms, so the return value does not depend on the branch and is unaffected by the free. The model test makes the free observer overwrite the object's first word and still requires the returned pointer to be the receiver, which rules out returning the object's current first word, a subobject, or the callee's return value.

semantic_findings: This is a deleting destructor, and the machine says so rather than the reconstruction: the immediate it stores at receiver+0x00 is 0x01489090, and the image word AT 0x01489090 is 0x00EC4280, this body's own entry point. That is slot +0x00 of a virtual function table holding this body, which on an x86-32 MSVC-style ABI is the scalar/vector deleting destructor slot.

The destructor has the three-arm signature of a multiple-inheritance class: vptr words at +0x00, +0x10 and +0x14, and two 10-byte this-adjusting thunks (0x00ec4230 with SUB ECX,0x10 and 0x00ec4240 with SUB ECX,0x14) that tail-jump into it, i.e. it is reached for receivers whose vptr words sit at those offsets.

The bit-0 test on a one-byte caller-supplied argument followed by a cdecl free of the receiver, guarded by a callee-popped RET 0x4, is the standard scalar deleting destructor shape. The flag byte's other seven bits are never read by this body and nothing here claims what they mean.

The three vptr stores this body performs are dead with respect to the final state: 0x00642190 overwrites the same three displacements with 0x013FF648 / 0x01462748 / 0x01462738 and then tail-transfers to 0x006412A0, which overwrites them a third time with 0x013EC458 / 0x013EB938 / 0x01403758. The stores exist for code that runs DURING the callee chain.

The flag byte is read after the callee returns, not on entry, and that ordering is observable precisely because the callee rewrites the surrounding object. The model preserves it with a hook at the read point rather than relying on the parameter, and the test overrides the hook to prove the arm follows the read.

The two arguments are the receiver and a delete-flag byte, and the receiver is returned -- a returning destructor, which is why Ghidra's 'undefined' return type is worth correcting rather than copying.

The 0x10 and 0x14 subobject adjustments exist only in the thunks. The body itself never adjusts its receiver, and both callees receive the receiver exactly as passed. Copying a thunk adjustment into this body would be wrong, and the test has a case for it.

unresolved_questions: What the class actually is. No MSVC RTTI survives in this binary (the repo's own AGENTS.md says so and the record's evidence_note repeats it), and no record names the class. The type name SporepediaOnlineAsset is for readability and is not a claim. The triage cluster says 'sporepedia-online' and the eight analogue records share this vftable, so the neighbourhood is Sporepedia, but the specific class and its bases are unknown.

Why 0x00EC4280 also appears at 0x0148907C + 0x14 and at 0x0148906C + 0x24, and why the thunks sit at 0x0148907C + 0x08 and 0x0148906C + 0x00. The three tables are consecutive in .rdata and their trailing entries are identical, which is consistent both with one class reachable through two base subobjects and with the linker simply laying related tables next to each other. The bytes do not decide it, so no slot boundary is modelled and no hierarchy is claimed.

What the other seven bits of the delete-flag byte mean, and who sets them. Only bit 0 is examined here. An MSVC deleting destructor normally encodes more than one condition in that byte, and this body is the only place in this package that can see it, so the question is genuinely open from this VA alone.

Whether the three bytes at entry_ESP+0x5..0x7 of the argument slot are ever non-zero in real callers. RET 0x4 fixes the slot's width and the 0xF6 r/m8 form fixes that only the low byte is read, but no caller was identified to check what it writes in the upper half.

Whether the return value is ever consumed. No caller is recorded for this VA (Ghidra lists callers [] and the only xrefs are the vtable word and the two thunks), so the returning destructor's contract -- whether a caller uses EAX, or whether this is a hand-rolled destructor rather than a compiler-emitted one -- cannot be settled from the image at this address.

The interior of 0x00642190 and of the 0x006412A0 chain. The five null-guarded indirect handle releases, the inline-vector comparison and the tail transfer are opaque seams here; this package asserts only the three vptr words, the terminator and the zero-argument convention, all of which were re-read from the image.
